definitions.explanation: The weight or force applied to a structure, machine, or surface. A technical term used in engineering, construction, and physics.

examples.japanese: {荷重|かじゅう}に{耐|た}える{設計|せっけい}。
examples.english: A design that withstands the load.

examples.japanese: {最大|さいだい}{荷重|かじゅう}は500キログラムだ。
examples.english: The maximum load capacity is 500 kilograms.

examples.japanese: {橋|はし}にかかる{荷重|かじゅう}を{計算|けいさん}して{安全性|あんぜんせい}を{確認|かくにん}する。
examples.english: We calculate the load on the bridge to verify its safety.

notes: Composed of {荷|か} (load, cargo) + {重|じゅう} (weight, heavy). A technical/engineering term referring to the force or weight applied to something, not the weight of the object itself. Common collocations: {荷重|かじゅう}をかける (to apply a load), {荷重|かじゅう}{制限|せいげん} (load limit), {最大|さいだい}{荷重|かじゅう} (maximum load), {荷重|かじゅう}{試験|しけん} (load test). Not to be confused with the homophone {果汁|かじゅう} (fruit juice). Types of {荷重|かじゅう}: {静荷重|せいかじゅう} (static load), {動荷重|どうかじゅう} (dynamic load), {風荷重|かぜかじゅう} (wind load), {雪荷重|ゆきかじゅう} (snow load).
